_meta.disclaimer: SkinScan provides general information, not a medical diagnosis. It does not replace a consultation with a qualified healthcare professional. Do not use this result to delay seeking medical care. If you are worried about your skin, see a clinician.
_meta.skinToneNote: SkinScan is being validated for South African skin tones. AI dermatology models are typically less accurate on darker skin (Fitzpatrick IV-VI). If your result looks wrong to you, trust your judgement and see a clinician.

emergency.question: Are you having trouble breathing or swallowing, or is there swelling of your eyes or lips?
emergency.message: This may be a severe allergic reaction. Call an ambulance or go to the nearest emergency department immediately.

urgent.question: Is the rash spreading over most of your body?
urgent.message: A rash covering most of the body needs same-day medical assessment.

urgent.question: Are there blisters, open sores, or raw, weeping skin?
urgent.message: Blisters or open skin can indicate infection or a drug reaction. See a clinic today.

urgent.question: Do you have a fever, or do you feel generally unwell with the rash?
urgent.message: A rash with fever needs same-day assessment to rule out infection or a systemic reaction.

urgent.question: Is the rash spreading quickly (noticeably worse within 24 hours)?
urgent.message: A rapidly spreading rash should be assessed today.

urgent.question: Is the rash painful rather than just itchy?
urgent.message: A painful rash may indicate infection or shingles. See a clinic today.

urgent.question: Does the rash involve your eyes, lips, mouth, or genital skin?
urgent.message: A rash on mucous membranes needs urgent medical assessment.

urgent.question: If you have eczema: has it suddenly become much more painful, with clusters of small blisters or punched-out sores?
urgent.message: This may be eczema herpeticum, a skin emergency. Go to a hospital or clinic immediately.

Acne.summary: A common condition of the hair follicles and oil glands. It can leave scars and dark marks if untreated, especially on darker skin.
Acne.symptoms: Blackheads and whiteheads, inflamed red bumps, pustules, and in severe cases deep painful nodules or cysts.

severityGuide.mild: Mostly blackheads and whiteheads, with few inflamed spots.
severityGuide.moderate: A mix of blackheads or whiteheads and inflamed red bumps or pustules.
severityGuide.severe: Widespread deep nodules or cysts, often painful, with prominent inflammation.

selfCare: Do not squeeze or pick spots - this increases scarring and dark marks.
Wash your face twice daily with a gentle cleanser. Over-washing makes it worse.
Avoid greasy or oil-based moisturisers and cosmetics that block follicles.
Use a non-comedogenic moisturiser and sunscreen - sun damage darkens acne marks.
A topical benzoyl peroxide product can help mild acne. It takes several weeks to work.
seeClinicIf: Acne is leaving scars or persistent dark marks.
Two 12-week courses of treatment have not worked.
Acne is affecting your mood, confidence, or daily life.
You have deep, painful nodules or cysts.

Eczema.summary: A chronic itchy skin condition that comes in flares. The skin barrier is weakened, so moisture escapes and irritants get in.
Eczema.symptoms: Dry, itchy, red patches. In flares: weeping, crusting, and thickened skin from scratching. Common on hands, inner elbows, behind knees, and face.
selfCare: Apply emollient (moisturiser) every day - during flares and when the skin looks clear.
Use soap-free washes instead of ordinary soap.
Avoid known irritants: harsh soaps, fragranced products, wool, and very hot water.
For red, inflamed patches, a short course of topical corticosteroid is the standard treatment. Use the lowest strength that controls the flare.
Keep nails short and avoid scratching - scratching worsens the barrier and increases infection risk.
seeClinicIf: Eczema is not controlled with daily emollients and a mild topical steroid.
There is recurrent infection (weeping, crusting, pustules, yellow discharge).
Eczema is causing significant distress, poor sleep, or missing school or work.
Eczema is widespread or affecting the face, hands, or genital area.
urgentIf: Rapidly worsening painful eczema with clustered blisters or punched-out erosions - possible eczema herpeticum. Same-day hospital assessment.

Psoriasis.summary: A chronic inflammatory condition that speeds up skin cell turnover, causing raised, scaly plaques. It is not contagious.
Psoriasis.symptoms: Well-defined red plaques with silvery-white scale. Common on elbows, knees, scalp, and lower back. May involve nails (pitting, separation) and joints.
selfCare: Keep the skin moisturised - dryness worsens scaling.
Use topical treatment on plaques as directed by a clinician (corticosteroid or vitamin D analogue preparations).
Avoid scratching or picking plaques - this can cause bleeding and infection.
Sunlight in moderation can help some people, but avoid sunburn.
Address factors that worsen psoriasis: smoking, excess alcohol, and excess weight.
seeClinicIf: Plaques are not improving after 4-8 weeks of topical treatment.
You have joint pain, stiffness, redness, or swelling - possible psoriatic arthritis.
Psoriasis is affecting your work, sleep, or social life.
urgentIf: Severe, widespread plaques with systemic symptoms (fever, feeling very unwell).
Generalised pustular psoriasis or erythroderma - emergency assessment.
